chapter: Inside the Basie rhythm section and band family
title: Lester Young's humor and life on the bus
summary: Lester was the funniest man in the band, calling men 'lady' and keeping the bus laughing; Basie rode with them.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well, listen. Just while we're talking about that band, I think we ought to talk -- take the different personalities and talk about them for a minute. I mean, there was Duckie I mean, he contributed -- I mean as a person --
Yes. As a person --
-- and as a stylist -- he contributed. I mean, he was a humorist.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
He made the guys laugh, didn't he? I mean, it was funny, wasn't it?
Well, I'll tell you one thing.
(laugh)
Lester Young was about the -- the humorous guy in the band.
Yeah.
tell me more.
He had some humor that you never heard before, you know. Funny things that he sings, and what-not
What kind of things? Can you remember?
He would say things right off the top of his head, more or less, you know. And, whatever it was -- you would have to laugh. You would have to laugh at them.
Do you remember a bell, or something that he rang? Or, what was that he used to do?
Yeah. Lester used to ring a bell on people. But, he used to do this, Freddie, remember?

Oh, yeah. He used to pull his -- lapel or something like that, you know. Little gestures he had -- that was there -- meant something, you know. (laugh) Oh, I can't think of -- there's so many of them, you know, that he had. Little things that he did.
All this business of calling men 'lady' was a funny thing, too.
'Lady', yeah. 'Lady' Jones, or anybody that he would come in contact with. He would say 'lady' this, and 'lady' that. You know what I mean. His reasons? I don't know.
There didn't have to be one. (laugh)

No. Not really. It's just funny, you know. And, that's it. I mean, he'd keep the bus laughing. He sat in the back of the bus at all times, and he would come up with some things. And, it was always a happy thing, you know, on the bus. Never a dull moment.
Did you play alot of cards?
Yeah. We played cards. Gambled. Did everything.
And, Basie always rode the bus?
(laugh) Yeah. He was always there.
Which is, you know -- that's really nice.
No, he stayed with us. He never ran off from us.
He didn't pull rank.
No, no. Never. He would never do that. Never has. Not as long as I've been there.
That's so exceptional, Stan, you know?
Always there.
